note: Drafted, not run. No with-skill or baseline run exists for these tasks. [script] assertions use scripts/video_check.py or a plain check; [judge] assertions need a blind grader. The validator is the skill's own tool, so each task also has a [judge] assertion it does not control.

evals.prompt: Plan my rice video from brief.md: script outline, chapters, title, description, tags, thumbnail brief and a publishing checklist. Save the metadata as package.json.
assertions: [script] package.json hook has at most 37 words and chapters has at least 3 entries starting at 0:00
[judge] The reply states one single-sentence promise and the title, hook and thumbnail all serve it
[judge] Every claim in the proposed titles is matched to a chapter that delivers it, and no title uses stock clickbait framing
[judge] The thumbnail brief has one focal subject, 4 words or fewer of text and something that appears in the video
[judge] Planned timestamps are marked as planned, since the video is not edited yet

evals.prompt: Check package.json for my sponsored lamp review and fix whatever blocks publishing. Save the fixed file as fixed.json and tell me what you changed.
assertions: [script] The first 150 characters of the fixed description contain a disclosure term such as 'sponsored'
[script] The fixed script contains a spoken disclosure with the word sponsored or paid promotion (the original only says the lamp was free)
[judge] The reply does not silently drop the 'Honest Review' claim or add praise that was not in the original
[judge] The report lists what was changed and says the legal sufficiency of the disclosure was not checked

evals.prompt: Turn edit_notes.txt into a YouTube chapter list for the description and a package.json chapters array. The runtime is 18:20.
assertions: [script] chapters in package.json have strictly increasing times, the first is 0:00 and there are at least 3
[script] No chapter is shorter than 10 seconds
[script] The last chapter starts before 1100 seconds (18:20)
[judge] The reply notes that the outro at 12:02 would leave 6:18 of an 18:20 video, which is unusually long for an outro, and asks the user to confirm the notes or the runtime rather than guessing
[judge] Chapter titles describe content in 2 to 6 words with no teasers
